en: The sampaguita, the national flower, is a species of jasmine scientifically known as Jasminum sambac.
The carabao, officially the national animal, is a domesticated swamp buffalo scientifically classified as Bubalus bubalis carabanesis.
The Banaue Rice Terraces, carved into mountains by the Ifugao people, use an ancient stone-walling irrigation system.
The Supreme Court, located in Manila, heads the judicial branch and interprets the Philippine Constitution.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered raptor endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
Filipino, the national language, is primarily based on Tagalog and incorporates words from other Philippine languages.
Filipino scientist Fe del Mundo founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines and invented a bamboo incubator.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño through a traditional two-steps-forward, one-step-back dance.
Under the 1987 Constitution, every Filipino citizen has the right to vote and the duty to pay taxes.
The Lumad are a collective group of indigenous peoples inhabiting the non-Muslim parts of Mindanao.
The South Sea pearl, the national gem, is a large pearl cultivated in the waters of Palawan.
